name: Trends.vc
tagline: Research reports on emerging markets and business ideas for founders

revenue.label: $20K MRR within a year of launch

timeToFirstDollar: 3 months (first report Feb 10, 2020; first paid revenue May 10, 2020)
summary: Trends.vc is a one-person research newsletter where Dru Riley publishes reports on one emerging market or trend at a time. Free readers get a summary and paid Trends Pro members get full reports and a community. He told the Indie Hackers podcast in September 2020 that it had reached $20K MRR in under a year, and it made $38,000 in October 2020.
origin: Riley, a software developer (Rails, Scala, Spark), quit his job in February 2017 with $250,000 in savings and went 37 months without income while traveling and trying projects. In fall 2019 he worked on a B2B SaaS marketing playbook and StrongStack, which he pivoted to SaaSReport in January 2020. To 'release steam' he started writing about trends and published the first Trends report, on cloud kitchens, on February 10, 2020.
howItMakesMoney: Trends Pro membership (full reports, databases, community, masterminds). The price went from $12/month in May 2020 to $149/year in August 2020 and $297/year in October 2020; Growth in Reverse listed the annual plan at $299/year in 2023. Sponsorships of the free newsletter were added in February 2022, and top reports are also sold as a bundle.
growth: Used a fixed, recognizable report format (Problem, Players, Predictions, Opportunities, Haters, Links) capped at 1,000 words
Tested the homepage email opt-in for months from May 2020, after seeing another founder report a 40% opt-in rate
Two Product Hunt launches produced the biggest jumps in subscribers; the first took the list from about 7,000 to 25,000 within days, and it reached #1 on Product Hunt in August 2020
Was active on Indie Hackers and in the Zero To One Makers mastermind, whose members shared the reports
Split each report into a free half and a paid half after a paid-only pre-order got zero sales
Raised prices several times as the report archive grew
moat: A large archive of researched reports and a paid community of founders; the format and consistency are hard to copy quickly.
risks: AI research tools can produce passable market summaries cheaply, pressuring the value of reports. Output depends on one researcher's time.

timeline.event: Quits software developer job to explore independent work
Works on StrongStack, pivoted to SaaSReport in January 2020
First Trends Pro revenue: $162 on the first day (May 10)
Reaches #1 on Product Hunt; makes about $24K that month
Tells Indie Hackers podcast he reached $20K MRR in under a year
Launches the Trends Pro community; earns $38,000 in the month
Adds sponsorships to the free newsletter

lessons: A strict, repeatable format makes a newsletter recognizable and faster to produce
Optimize the signup page before spending effort on traffic
Sell depth to the most engaged 1-2% of readers and keep summaries free
Failed products can point to what you actually enjoy producing

rebuild.idea: A paid research newsletter on emerging opportunities in one industry vertical, e.g. independent pharmacies or small manufacturing, with supplier and regulation data
rebuild.why: General founder-trend newsletters are crowded, but owners in traditional industries lack concise research on shifts affecting them and will pay for it.
mvp: Publish 3 free reports and post them in industry groups and forums
Put a signup page up and test headlines until a clear conversion rate is found
Offer a paid tier with full data tables for $20-30/month after report 4
rebuild.fit: An analyst or consultant with background in that industry
rebuild.pricing: Free summary newsletter with a paid tier at $20-30/month or $199-$299/year for full reports and data tables, plus one-off report sales around $49.
rebuild.market: Buyers are owners and operators in the chosen vertical (e.g. independent pharmacy owners), reached through trade associations, industry Facebook and LinkedIn groups, and conference talks. Competitors are trade publications and associations' member reports, general newsletters such as Trends.vc and Exploding Topics, and AI research tools.
